title: Nvidia and Cisco unveil next-gen network interface built for the AI data center boom
source_used: SiliconANGLE (guest column by Zeus Kerravala, ZK Research)
key_facts: At the Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose, Cisco showed a new pluggable optics form factor developed with Nvidia, called USFP (Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable).
USFP is the first pluggable module designed for 400-gigabit-per-lane signalling, up to 12.8 Tbps, about four times the bandwidth density of today's leading modules.
It is being standardised as a multisource agreement with TE Connectivity and Amphenol.
Cisco says the rival XPO approach needs liquid cooling, which no optic needs today.
Cisco also shipped its first Silicon One G300 systems and introduced the G302 top-of-rack chip.
The largest AI clusters now use hundreds of thousands of GPUs, so network slowdowns leave costly GPUs idle.
